key_insight: The quantum switch offers provable query advantages over definite-order circuits: exact simulation of general channels is impossible with finitely many calls in the worst case.
engineering_relevance: Its ability to distinguish noise models with identical entanglement and average gate fidelities could inform noise characterization for quantum error correction.
method: Analyze circuit-model simulation of coherently controlled operation orders.
Prove query lower bounds allowing classical feed-forward and unlimited ancillary quantum memory.
Compare unknown-basis dephasing with a theoretical depolarizing channel.
evidence_signal: Theoretical bounds show Ω(d^{1/4}) calls for simulation below 1/2 half-diamond-norm error and Ω(d^{1/16}) for noise discrimination, versus dimension-independent switch uses for the latter.
watch_item: The abstract establishes theoretical query advantages, not experimentally validated performance gains under realistic implementation overheads.
paper_title: Infinite or indefinite: the query cost of simulating the quantum switch
